draft.title: The First World War and Russia
card: Russia entered the First World War in 1914 against Germany and Austria-Hungary. At first, patriotic crowds backed the tsar.
Russian armies lost major battles, such as Tannenberg in 1914. Millions of soldiers were killed, wounded or captured, and many lacked enough rifles, boots and shells.
Farm workers and horses went to the army, and the railways were clogged with military traffic. Food and fuel reached the cities in small amounts, so prices rose and queues grew.
In 1915 Nicholas II took personal command of the army. After that, the tsar was blamed for each defeat and for the hardship at home.
draft.remember: War losses and shortages turned early support for the tsar into blame.

a.q: Why did the war cost Nicholas II support from ordinary Russians?
opts: Defeats and shortages were blamed on his rule
Victories made the army more powerful than him
Peasants refused to pay tax to fund the war
Russia's allies demanded that he give up power
a.why: Heavy losses at the front and hunger at home were blamed on the tsar, especially after he took command of the army in 1915. The tempting option about victories is wrong because Russia suffered major defeats.
a.clue: Think about who was blamed when things went wrong.

b.q: Lena lives in Petrograd in 1916. Bread is scarce and her brother was killed at the front. Which fact about the tsar most directly links her two troubles to him?
opts: He had taken personal command of the army in 1915
He had called an election for the Duma in 1906
He had signed a peace treaty with Germany in 1914
He had sold farmland to peasants in 1910
b.why: Once Nicholas II led the army himself, he could be blamed for the defeats and losses, and for a war that strained food supplies. The other options do not match the card: Russia was still fighting Germany, and the card does not link land sales or the Duma to the war.
b.clue: Which choice ties the tsar to the war itself?

a.best: Defeats and shortages were blamed on his rule

b.best: He had taken personal command of the army in 1915

check.summary: No problems found. The dates for the start of the war, Tannenberg (1914) and Nicholas II taking command (1915) are accurate, and each question has one clearly right answer that the card supports.
